description:
FOUND + FIXED (code written, BARS UNRUN) s461ar, agent AR, round 18.  The
change is in the worktree agent-ab82dbae53145b914 and is UNVERIFIED beyond two
probes -- see "STATE" at the end.

TWO BUGS, ONE FAMILY.  Both are about the #351 `WORD /` derail, whose damage is
UNBOUNDED in exactly the way `_repair_glob_pattern_cascade`'s is: PPI reads the
`/` after a paren-less call as DIVISION, scans for a closing `/`, and having
passed it is back in term position -- so the NEXT `/` opens a `Regexp::Match`
that swallows every statement in between.

(a) `_repair_word_match` RAN ONCE where it must run TO FIXPOINT.  Repro:

    sub ok { print "ok: $_[0] $_[1]\n"; }
    $_ = 'aaabccc';
     ok /a+b?c+/, "one";
     ok /a*b?c*/, "two";
    print "done\n";

The second `ok` is not a Word token at all -- it is text inside
`Regexp::Match</, "one";\n ok /a>` -- so pass 1 repairs line 3 and line 4 is
only a `WORD /` site AFTER that pass's reparse.  perl prints three lines; PCL
printed one and dropped the rest.  `_repair_glob_pattern_cascade` was given the
identical fixpoint loop in s449 for the identical reason; this one was missed.
FIX: split into `_repair_word_match` (a bounded 20-round loop) and
`_repair_word_match_pass` (the old body, returning undef when it changed
nothing) -- the same two-sub shape the glob cascade uses.

(b) THE REPAIR ORDER WAS WRONG, and (a)'s fix exposed it.  With the fixpoint in
place the statement stopped dropping but the pattern came out as
`m/a* b?c*/` -- a SPACE spliced into the middle of a regex, so it matched
something else and the row silently changed answer (`ok: 1 two` -> `ok:  two`).
Cause: `_repair_glob_multiply` (#354) ran BEFORE `_repair_word_match`, met the
`*b` of `a*b?c*` as a `PPI::Token::Symbol` (a Regexp ends a term, so its
`_ends_term` guard passed) and rewrote it to `* b`.  It was reading PATTERN
TEXT tokenized as code.  FIX: `_repair_word_match` moves up to run SECOND in
the repair block, immediately after `_repair_glob_pattern_cascade` and before
`_repair_glob_multiply`, under the same stated principle -- a repair whose
damage is unbounded must run before the repairs that read the damaged region,
never beside them.

MEASURED: with both halves the repro is byte-identical to perl 5.40.3
(`ok: 1 one` / `ok: 1 two` / `done`).  Census owner: `t/re/pat.t:106`, whose
one drop swallowed three statements including a `$_ = 'aaaccc'` reset.

  * NO `docs/ppi-upstream-bugs.md` section and NO `docs/ppi-bug-report.t` row.

  * Generation NOT bumped and the three artifacts NOT regenerated.
